summary: GitHub App claim window race causes worker pods to fail registering during KMS rewrap
description:
Issue summary:
- During a planned KMS rewrap and Vault transit key rotation a subset of ephemeral worker pods failed to claim GitHub App installation tokens and remained in a "pending/CrashLoopBackOff" state. The failure window corresponds to the rewrap and subsequent short TTL mismatch between Vault response and the runner controller.

Impact:
- Multiple release jobs in the nightly cutover failed (approx 18 jobs) and several release gates were delayed by ~45-90 minutes. This affected internal release pipelines only (no customer-facing endpoints).

Environment:
- Prod cluster: k8s: cluster-autoscaler v1.30, runner controller v2.4.1, Vault transit rewrap initiated from infra-ops in us-west-2.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Trigger Vault transit rewrap of the "github-app-transit" key with short rolling window.
2. Start a burst of ephemeral runner pod bootstraps (concurrent 120 pods).
3. Watch controller logs: tokens returned by Vault sometimes have an issuance timestamp that is ahead of controller's lease table leading to immediate rejection on claim validation.

Observed behavior:
- ~15% of pods failed to progress past "Init" and logged 403/invalid-claim-like errors from GitHub App token exchange. Some pods retried and succeeded after 30-60s; a cohort never recovered without manual restart.

Expected behavior:
- Controller should accept the token issuance window despite small clock skew / token epoch drift during coordinated rewrap and should queue or retry gracefully rather than leaving pods unregistered.

Logs / artifacts:
- controller logs (snippet):
  2026-02-25T01:12:03Z controller runner claim: token-claim failed validation: issuance_ts 2026-02-25T01:12:05Z > lease_epoch 2026-02-25T01:12:03Z
- Vault audit: transit rewrap started 2026-02-25T01:11:59Z, rewrap completed 2026-02-25T01:12:04Z.
- GitHub App exchange traces: 403 entries correlated to pod ids: runner-7f9c, runner-8g2p, runner-93kd.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: clock skew between controller nodes and Vault caused tokens to appear issued in the future relative to controller's lease table.
Checked NTP/chrony across controller fleet — clocks within 20ms, so not a pure NTP drift issue.
Observed that Vault returned tokens stamped with microsecond-level future timestamps occasionally due to async rewrap commit ordering in transit plugin.
Controller compares token.issuance_ts against its local lease_epoch and rejects if issuance_ts > lease_epoch + acceptance_window (currently 0s).
Reproduced locally by running a mini rewrap and starting 200 ephemeral bootstraps — saw similar 403s when issuance_ts skew > 30ms.
Traffic pattern: burst of concurrent claims amplifies race because some controller workers update lease_epoch only after their local cache refresh; tokens minted in-between fail validation.
Controller code path: token validation occurs in claim_validation.go, function ValidateTokenEpoch. Acceptance window is hardcoded to 0 and should be configurable.
SRE mitigations tested: manual leader restart + controller cache flush allowed stuck pods to complete registration; suggests caching/timing problem rather than permanent token invalidity.

2026-02-25 02:22 - Infra Ops (Marta Li): Confirmed Vault transit rewrap was scheduled and executed at 01:12 UTC. No other Vault anomalies reported. Collecting audit logs.

2026-02-25 03:10 - Diego Morales (SRE): Ran quick mitigation — bumped controller acceptance window to 100ms and rolled a hotfix to the controller group. Majority of stuck pods recovered within 20 minutes.

2026-02-25 04:30 - Platform Eng (Ravi Singh): Created short-lived feature flag to make acceptance_window configurable. Preparing PR to fix ValidateTokenEpoch logic to tolerate up to 2s jitter with exponential backoff on failures.
2026-02-25 05:15 - QA (Nora): Confirmed that restart of controller leader clears pending pods; adding e2e to reproduce burst registration during rewrap in staging.

2026-03-02 11:00 - Diego Morales: Follow-up: ran canary with simulated rewrap in staging. New logic accepted slightly-future tokens and retried failed claims; no stuck pods observed in 5 runs. Planning rollout to prod 2026-03-04.
2026-03-03 09:20 - Aisha Patel: Flagging follow-up items to CI runbook and postmortem; inform release coordinators about increased acceptance window behavior.
resolution:
Workaround applied: hotfix changed controller acceptance window to 100ms and performed a rolling restart of controller replicas. Manual restart of affected runner pods recovered remaining stuck jobs.

Permanent fix plan: (1) PR merged to make acceptance window configurable and add exponential retry/backoff in ValidateTokenEpoch (PR#12245), (2) controller will refresh lease_epoch before rejecting a claim and will enqueue claims that fail soft validation for 2s retry, (3) update runbook with steps for coordinated Vault rewrap (add pre-roll cache flush and graceful restart), (4) infra-ops to stagger rewraps or use a cross-cluster rekey plan for high-concurrency periods.

Postmortem action items assigned: Diego (implement and roll out fix), Ravi (merge PR and add e2e), Marta (update Vault rewrap runbook), Aisha (communicate to release ops).
next_steps: Rollout PR#12245 to prod during low-traffic window on 2026-03-04 (Diego/Ravi).
Add an automated stage in the Vault rewrap runbook to pause large ephemeral bootstrap waves for 5 minutes (Marta).
Add e2e test to CI that simulates high-concurrency bootstrap during transit rewrap and assert no stuck pods (Ravi/Nora).
Notify Release Coordinators of mitigation and updated runbook (Aisha).
